subject: Timeline slip containment raft and MAP handback request
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft — emerging blocker, potential 2-week slip

Hi Stephanie,

Quick update from our side — thanks for the MAP draft. We ran into a security gating item this morning: our InfoSec requires an integration runbook and a signed acceptance of data-retention limits before the eval cluster can be scheduled. That paperwork was expected this week but will now take until next Friday (we were told by SecOps).

Practically this means the acceptance window you and I penciled for 4/22 will slip by ~10–14 business days unless we change the MAP. We know that affects your delivery commitments and internal routing.

Options on our side:
- Push the eval start by two weeks and keep current scope, or
- Run a narrow smoke evaluation with anonymized test data next week (reduced scope) while security completes sign-off.

Can you outline how Redwood would prefer to handle the MAP update and any implications on reserved capacity or credits? We have an exec call Monday and would like to propose a single, simple path.

Apologies for the last-minute note — SecOps only escalated this morning.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Senior Program Manager | Greenline Health

Attachments: none
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft — emerging blocker, potential 2-week slip

Hi Maya — thanks for the heads up and for outlining the two options.

Short answer: both are feasible, we prefer the narrow smoke eval as a contingency since it preserves some forward momentum and minimizes pressure on the reserved capacity. That said, we recognize you may prefer a clean rebaseline. Two immediate asks from our side:

1) If you pick the smoke eval path, can SecOps confirm the anonymization approach (types of data removed) so we validate ingestion and metric parity?
2) If you pick the two-week push, we need to update the MAP and confirm whether Greenline expects any credit/discount for the compressed runway cost increase.

I'm looping in Aditya (procurement/support) to flag any implications for dedicated capacity and crediting. He can advise on what we can offer as a containment "raft" (short-term measures: burst capacity hold, temporary reduced-rate allocation) while we update the MAP.

Options for the call on Monday: I can propose the smoke eval + conditional rebaseline if SecOps needs more time. If you'd like I can also prepare a short risk log to identify top three failure modes and the suggested mitigations.

I'll follow up internally and send a formal MAP handback proposal by EOD.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: acceptance-window-proposal.pdf (stub)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP draft — emerging blocker, potential 2-week slip

Team — forwarding Greenline note. TL;DR: security gating will likely push the eval start ~10–14 business days unless we run a narrow anonymized smoke eval next week.

Why I need you:
- Aditya: can you confirm whether we can stand up a temporary "containment raft" — a short burst allocation and a one-time credit/discount to keep the committed date intact if they choose the push? Also, what approvals do we need to offer a partial credit?
- Ben: can you advise on the operational feasibility of a smoke eval that excludes PHI fields (anonymized CSV ingestion) and whether that materially changes our effort estimate?

I'm attaching a quick risk log (map-risk-log.xlsx) with the three most-likely failure modes and proposed mitigations. If we get sign-off on a small credit and the smoke eval route, I want to send Maya a single-page MAP handback that:
- Updates acceptance window (conditional on SecOps finish) OR
- Approves smoke eval next week with clearly scoped success criteria (ingest, latency, sample prompts).

Please reply with feasibility and a one-line approval or the required escalation path. Monday exec call is the decision point; we need something by COB Monday.

Thanks — Stephanie

Attachment: map-risk-log.xlsx (stub)
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: program@greenlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Timeline slip containment raft and MAP handback request

Stephanie — following our exec call, we want to proceed with the smoke eval next week to avoid a hard two-week push. SecOps confirmed the anonymization checklist (removed PII/PHI columns, tokenized IDs) and are comfortable with the limited-scope run under that condition.

Greenline asks the following from Redwood:
- A short MAP handback that replaces the original acceptance window with: "Conditional smoke eval week of 4/19; full eval window begins week of 5/3 pending SecOps sign-off."
- The smoke eval success criteria (ingestion of anonymized dataset, <200ms avg latency for sample prompts, and end-to-end traceability for five test cases).
- Confirmation of a one-time containment credit applied if the full eval must be pushed beyond 5/3 due to SecOps (we are open to a 50% discount on the first week's reserved capacity if delay > 7 business days).

If you can get me the MAP handback and the high-level success criteria before 9am PT Tuesday, we'll sign and proceed with the smoke eval. Appreciate you mobilizing quickly here.

Thanks,
Maya
Senior Program Manager | Greenline Health

Forwarded headers included above where relevant."
